notes.title: -기 시작하다
notes.text: -기 시작하다 means "to start doing": 어두워지기 시작했어요 (it started getting dark), 눈이 내리기 시작했어요 (it started to snow). On New Year's Eve, Seoul gathers for the midnight bell at 보신각 or for fireworks along the Han River. 새해 복 많이 받으세요! = Happy New Year! (literally "receive lots of luck in the new year")

notes.title: Seollal
notes.text: 설날 (Lunar New Year) is Korea's biggest holiday. Families wear 한복 and eat 떡국 (rice cake soup — eating it makes you a year older!). Younger family members bow deeply to elders (세배) and receive 세뱃돈 (New Year's money) and good wishes. 정 is a very Korean word for the deep, warm bond between people who share their lives.

notes.title: -(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라
notes.text: -(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 means "not only… but also": 종류를 늘릴 뿐만 아니라 가게도 열 거예요. With nouns: 할머니뿐만 아니라 지우도 (not only Grandma but Ji-woo too). New Year's resolutions are 새해 계획 or 새해 결심.

talk.en: Are you going back to America?

talk.cue: Say you want to keep living in Korea.

notes.title: Moving forward
notes.text: 나서다 (to set out, step forward), 들어서다 (to step in, move in), 앞서다 (to go ahead, come before), 맞서다 (to face, stand up to). 포기하지 마세요! (Don't give up!) is one of the most encouraging things you can say in Korean — to Jamie, and to you.

lessons.goal: Look back on the year together.

scene.ko: 그날 밤, 별과 서연이 스케치북에 새 그림을 그려요. 한편 민준은 상을 차리고, 할머니는 꽃을 갈아요.
scene.en: That night, Byeol and Seo-yeon draw a new picture in the sketchbook. Meanwhile, Min-jun sets the table and Grandma changes the flowers.
b: to set (a table), to prepare (a meal)

scene.en: Jamie draws carefully: the boarding house, Grandma, Min-jun, Seo-yeon, Ji-woo, Byeol, Do-yoon — and the puppy. A whole family.

scene.ko: 할머니, 이 그림 학교에 가져가도 돼요? 어린이날에 친구들한테 보여 줄래요!
scene.en: Grandma, can I take this picture to school? I want to show my friends on Children's Day!
b: to become; to work, to be okay (돼요)

scene.en: Of course. My heart feels at ease now. This is all I wish for — that we all stay healthy, together.

notes.text: 축하해요! You've reached the end of 별빛 하숙집 — 40 units and roughly 3,000 of the most useful Korean words. Keep going: review a little every day, watch Korean shows with Korean subtitles, and talk with people. 앞으로도 화이팅! (Keep it up from here!)
